_note: Genshin jargon for /genshin-impact/glossary (genshin-glossary.js). Picked from the Genshin Impact Wiki's community Glossary (Fandom, CC BY-SA, 338 terms) for what players use most and newcomers ask about; facts checked against the wiki's Wish, Team Bonus and Damage pages, Oct 26 2026 (7.1). id = permanent (#t-<id> links). also = other spellings (searched too). ex = an example line. see = related ids. link = a Parchrome page that explains more. hot = shown in Most asked. Decoder lines: [text, id] pairs, id = '' for plain text.

terms.def: How many wishes since your last 5★ (or 4★) on a banner. It counts toward a guaranteed drop. Each banner type keeps its own count; the two character banners share one, and it carries over to the next banner of that type.
terms.ex: I'm sitting on 60 pity, saving for the next rerun.

terms.def: The point where the 5★ chance starts climbing with every wish: around wish 74 on character banners, 63 on the weapon banner. HoYoverse never named it; players worked it out from millions of wishes. Most 5★s land in this stretch.
terms.ex: Got her at 76, right in soft pity.

terms.def: The wish that can't miss: the 90th on character banners and the Standard banner, the 80th on the weapon banner.
terms.ex: Hard pity again. 90 wishes for one 5★.

terms.def: When a 5★ drops on a character banner, it's either the featured character or one from the standard pool. Win and the next 5★ is a 50/50 again; lose and the next one is guaranteed to be featured.
terms.ex: Lost my 50/50 to Diluc. Again.

terms.def: After losing a 50/50, your next 5★ on a character banner is the featured one. The guarantee carries over to later banners, so you can save it for the character you want.
terms.ex: I'm on guarantee, so the next 5★ is hers.

terms.def: Since Version 5.0, a hidden boost on the 50/50: it can flip a loss into the featured character, so the real odds are 55%, not 50%. Lose the 50/50 three times in a row and the next one is a sure win. It never touches a guarantee.
terms.ex: Capturing Radiance just saved my 50/50.

terms.def: The weapon banner's version of the 50/50: a 5★ weapon there is one of the two featured weapons 75% of the time. Miss and the next one is featured for sure.
terms.ex: Lost the 75/25 to Wolf's Gravestone.

terms.def: Pick one of the two featured weapons. Every 5★ that isn't it gives you a Fate Point; with one point, the next 5★ is your pick. At worst that's 160 wishes for one specific weapon.
terms.ex: Set the path before your first weapon wish, or the point doesn't count.

terms.def: Ten wishes at once. Same odds as ten singles, just faster: the game's 4★ guarantee (one every 10 wishes) works either way.
terms.ex: One multi, three blues and a Xiangling.

terms.def: Primogems, the premium currency. 160 buy one wish, as an Intertwined Fate (limited banners) or an Acquaint Fate (Standard banner).
terms.ex: Saved 14k primos for the rerun.

terms.def: Primogems you earn by playing: quests, Commissions, events, the Abyss, codes. Apologems are the ones HoYoverse sends as compensation for bugs and maintenance.
terms.ex: Free-to-play is all freemogems.

terms.def: A character's banner coming back after the first one. The wait between reruns can be a year or more.
terms.ex: Skipping her first run, I'll get her on rerun.

terms.def: An Event Wish, named after its featured 5★: "the Furina banner". Two character banners usually run at once, plus the weapon banner and the Chronicled Wish now and then.
A 5★ character's signature weapon, the one released with them and made for their kit.
terms.ex: Her sig is great, but not a must.

terms.def: A character with all six Constellations holding their weapon at Refinement 5: as far as an account can push one character. It takes around 7 copies of the character and 5 of the weapon.
terms.ex: Whales flexing C6R5 in co-op again.

terms.def: A player who never spends money on the game. "F2P friendly" means a character or weapon works without paid copies.
A player who spends big. Dolphins spend a moderate amount; goldfish only buy the Welkin or the Battle Pass.
The monthly pass: 300 Genesis Crystals when you buy it, then 90 Primogems a day for 30 days. Widely seen as the best value in the shop.
The Battle Pass. The free track gives materials; the paid one (Gnostic Hymn) adds a 4★ weapon pick, Fates and more.
How many Constellations a character has. Every extra copy you pull unlocks one, up to six. C0 = just the character.
terms.ex: C0 is fine, C2 is where she gets scary.

terms.def: A weapon's Refinement rank. Each extra copy of the weapon you feed it raises its passive, up to R5.
terms.ex: R5 means four extra copies went into it.

terms.def: A character's Ascension phase (A0 to A6). A1 and A4 usually mean the two passive talents unlocked at those phases.
terms.ex: Her A4 passive unlocks at the level 70 ascension.

terms.def: Talents go from 1 to 10; Constellations 3 and 5 add 3 more, up to 13. Players write them Normal Attack / Skill / Burst: "1/9/9" means level 1 Normal Attack, 9 Skill, 9 Burst.
terms.ex: Support, so 1/9/9 is plenty.

terms.def: Spending a Crown of Insight to take a talent from 9 to 10. A triple crown = all three combat talents at 10. Crowns are rare: a few a year.
terms.ex: Finally crowned her Skill.

terms.def: Materials for levelling and ascending: talent books (domains on set days), boss drops, local specialties.
The best weapon or artifact set for a character. Often a 5★ weapon; rarely needed to clear anything.
terms.ex: Her BiS is her sig, but Deathmatch is close.

terms.def: The five artifact slots: Flower (HP), Feather or Plume (ATK), then the three with a choice of main stat: Sands (timepiece), Goblet (cup) and Circlet (hat).
Shorthand for the Sands / Goblet / Circlet main stats: ATK% Sands, Pyro DMG Goblet, Crit Circlet. ADC = ATK/DMG/Crit; EDC = EM/DMG/Crit.
terms.ex: ER/Hydro/Crit if she's short on energy.

terms.def: An artifact's four smaller stats under the main one. Every 4 levels one of them gets a random boost, a roll. Good subs (Crit, the right %) make or break a build.
terms.ex: Crit Circlet with flat DEF subs. Fodder.

terms.def: Artifact set bonuses: two pieces of a set unlock its first effect, four unlock the second. "2+2" means two sets of two.
terms.ex: 4pc VV on any Anemo support.

terms.def: The fifth artifact that doesn't match your 4pc set, worn because its stats are better.
terms.ex: Off-piece Circlet, 30 CV, keeping it.

terms.def: Five artifacts from different sets: no set bonus, just stats. Also a team of four different elements.
terms.ex: Rainbow set until the domain gives me something.

terms.def: A quick score for how much crit something has: Crit DMG + 2 × Crit Rate. Used to judge an artifact's substats (or a whole build) at a glance.
terms.ex: That's a 40 CV Feather, frame it.

terms.def: The rule of thumb for crit: about twice as much Crit DMG as Crit Rate, like 70% / 140%. It gets the most damage out of a given amount of crit.
How much of an artifact's possible upgrades landed on the stats you want, as a percentage of a perfect roll.
Crit Rate over 100%, which does nothing extra. Also used for Resin past its 200 cap.
terms.ex: She's at 115% with the buff: overcapped.

terms.def: Running very low Crit Rate with huge Crit DMG and resetting until the big hit crits. Fine for a screenshot, bad for real play.
Plain-number substats (+19 ATK) instead of percentages (+5.8% ATK). Usually the weakest roll on an artifact.
A weapon used only for its main stat, its passive doing nothing for that character.
Energy Recharge: how fast a Burst charges. "ER requirement" = how much a character needs to have their Burst ready every rotation.
terms.ex: Check her ER requirement before you swap to an ATK Sands.

terms.def: Elemental Mastery: makes reactions hit harder. Each reaction family gets a different curve from it.
The character who deals most of the team's damage, usually on the field the longest.
A character who deals real damage but isn't the main one, often from off-field: their Skill or Burst keeps hitting after you swap.
On-field = the character you're playing. Off-field = the other three, whose summons and buffs keep working after you swap. Field time = how long a character needs to stay in.
terms.ex: Xingqiu is all off-field: Burst, swap out.

terms.def: The on-field character whose fast hits keep triggering the off-field characters' damage and reactions.
terms.ex: Bineffa needs a driver with fast Hydro.

terms.def: A character who makes a reaction team work, usually by putting an element on enemies all the time.
A character whose main job is to make Energy particles for the rest of the team.
terms.ex: Fischl is the battery, Raiden swaps in full.

terms.def: A team built so one character deals almost all the damage, the other three only buffing and enabling them.
A playstyle where every character pops in for a Skill or Burst and swaps out: lots of off-field damage, little field time each.
Two or three off-field characters who do so much for a team that nearly anyone works in the last slot. They "carry" the team the way a wheelchair carries its rider.
terms.ex: Bineffa is a wheelchair: throw anyone in.

terms.def: A support built only for their shield (or heals, for a healbot), skipping damage. "-bot" after a role means "used only for" it.
A team slot several characters can fill. Also: showing off what you pulled.
Team composition: the four characters in a party.
The two or three characters that make a team work; the rest is flexible. Also short for Dendro Cores.
The order you press every Skill and Burst in a team, until they're all back off cooldown and you repeat.
terms.ex: E Q, swap, E, swap, E Q: that's the rotation.

terms.def: How much of a rotation a buff or skill is active. 100% uptime = never off. Downtime = the gap while it's on cooldown.
Making Energy particles with one character, then swapping to another to catch them, so the second one gets their Burst back faster.
Some lasting skills lock your stats at the moment you cast them: buffs that end later still count. Dynamic skills update with your current stats instead.
A character you rarely use any more, usually because someone newer does the job better.
The characters and teams the community considers strongest right now, mostly judged by Abyss and Theater clears.
Xiangling, Xingqiu and Bennett plus a fourth: one of the oldest and cheapest strong teams. International swaps Childe in for Xingqiu; Rational puts Raiden in the fourth slot.
An Electro-Charged team, classically Sucrose, Fischl, Beidou and Xingqiu.
The classic Freeze team: Mona, Ganyu, Diona and Venti (Mo-Gan-a). Permafreeze = any team that keeps enemies frozen nearly all the time.
Vape = Vaporize. Forward = the 2× side (Hydro on Pyro, Pyro on Cryo), reverse = the 1.5× side (Pyro on Hydro, Cryo on Pyro).
A team that makes Dendro Cores with Bloom and turns them into homing shots with Electro. Salad = a Hyperbloom team with an Anemo character.
A team of mostly one element, hitting with raw damage instead of reactions.
Columbina and Ineffa together: an off-field Lunar-Charged core strong enough to be called a wheelchair.
A hidden limit on how often an attack can apply its element. Most attacks apply it on the first hit, then only every third hit or once 2.5 s have passed, whichever comes first.
terms.ex: Her Skill has no ICD, so it reacts on every hit.

terms.def: The element already sitting on an enemy. The trigger is the second element that hits it and starts the reaction. Most reactions use the trigger's stats; Lunar ones blend everyone's.
How strong an element application is (1U, 2U, 4U). Bigger units last longer and survive more reactions. EGT = Elemental Gauge Theory, the community's model of it.
Lowering an enemy's resistance or defence, like VV or Superconduct. It makes every hit of that type land harder.
The tiny freeze when a melee hit connects. It pauses the attacker's timers too, which shifts how long some buffs last.
The moments an animation makes you untouchable, mostly during a dash and some Bursts.
Cutting an attack's end animation short with a dash, jump or walk, so the next move starts sooner.
Attack-string shorthand: N = Normal Attack (N3 = three in a row), C = Charged Attack, D = dash, J = jump, P = plunge.
terms.ex: Her combo is N2C, dash, repeat.

terms.def: Skill and Burst, named after their PC keys. tE = tap Skill, hE = hold Skill.
terms.ex: Hold E, Q, swap.

terms.def: Plunging Attack damage: the hit you deal falling from above.
When a passive or effect triggers. "Favonius procced" = its particles dropped.
Area of Effect (hits a group) against Single Target (hits one enemy).
Any buff that adds flat damage to each hit, named after Shenhe's Icy Quill. It works like Aggravate and Spread do.
The % in a talent's description: how much of your ATK (or HP, DEF, EM) one hit deals.
Your account level, up to 60. It unlocks quests, domains and modes, and pushes your World Level up.
How tough your world is. It rises with AR: higher = stronger enemies, better drops. Co-op friends see your World Level in your world.
The stamina you spend on domains, bosses and ley lines. 1 comes back every 8 minutes, up to 200. Capped = full, so you're wasting what would refill.
terms.ex: Woke up resin capped. Again.

terms.def: Dailies = the four Daily Commissions. Weeklies = the weekly bosses and other once-a-week rewards.
When the game day turns over: 04:00 server time, not midnight. Weeklies reset on Monday.
The Spiral Abyss. Numbers are Floor-Chamber-Half: 12-3-2 = Floor 12, Chamber 3, second half. 36 stars = a full clear.
terms.ex: 12-3-1 is a DPS check.

terms.def: Imaginarium Theater: a monthly mode with a cast of characters you choose under set elements, each usable twice. Opens at AR 35.
Stygian Onslaught: a timed boss challenge mode with difficulty tiers, opened at AR 20.
Clearing a chamber (or boss) within one rotation of the team.
terms.ex: One rotate 12-3 with C0s.

terms.def: A region's Reputation level, raised by its bounties and requests. It unlocks blueprints and handy gadgets.
A Statue of The Seven: heals the party, revives fallen characters and clears Bond of Life.
Nod-Krai's team bonus. Each Moonsign character in the party raises it: one = Nascent Gleam, two or more = Ascendant Gleam, which powers up their talents and lets everyone else buff Lunar damage.
terms.ex: Two Moonsign units, so Ascendant Gleam is up.

terms.def: Lunar-Charged and Lunar-Bloom (Lunar-Crystallize is the third). Stronger versions of Electro-Charged, Bloom and Crystallize that a Moon Wheel user or Columbina swaps in. They can crit.
What some Nod-Krai characters (and Zibai) carry instead of a Vision. Moon Wheel users are the ones who turn Lunar reactions on.
Snezhnaya's Cryo reactions, Stellar-Conduct and Stellar Swirl, swapped in by Stellar Linchpin users and the Cryo Traveler.

Hexerei: a team bonus for characters tied to the Hexenzirkel witches (Albedo, Fischl, Klee, Mona, Sucrose, Venti and more). Finish a character's Witch's Homework quest to make them Hexerei; two in the party unlock Secret Rite and extra talent effects.
Nod-Krai's two artifact sets for Lunar teams: Night of the Sky's Unveiling and Silken Moon's Serenade. Both raise Lunar-Charged and Lunar-Bloom damage.

Natlan's Nightsoul: a powered-up state its characters enter. With a Natlan character in the party, dealing Elemental DMG also sets off a Nightsoul Burst, on a cooldown that shortens with each Natlan character you bring.
Bond of Life: a red bar over HP that soaks up healing until it's cleared. Some enemies put it on you; some characters put it on themselves for power.
Miliastra Wonderland: Genshin's player-made levels. UGC = user-generated content. Stages are built in the Miliastra Sandbox (PC only).
Nod-Krai, the region of the Luna versions (6.0 to 6.7), home of the Moon Wheels and Lunar reactions.
Viridescent Venerer: the Anemo support set. 4pc: Swirl DMG +60%, and enemies lose 40% resistance to the swirled element for 10 s.
Emblem of Severed Fate: Burst DMG goes up by 25% of your Energy Recharge, up to +75%.
Noblesse Oblige: Burst DMG +20%, and after a Burst the whole party gets +20% ATK for 12 s.
Crimson Witch of Flames: Pyro DMG, plus +40% Overloaded, Burning and Burgeon and +15% Vaporize and Melt.
Fontaine's sets: Golden Troupe boosts Skill DMG (off-field most), Marechaussee Hunter boosts Normal and Charged Attacks with Crit Rate whenever HP changes.

also: Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City
terms.def: Natlan's sets: Obsidian Codex for Nightsoul damage dealers, Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City for the supports who trigger reactions.
Two 4★ weapon series built for supports. Favonius crits drop Energy particles; Sacrificial can reset your Skill's cooldown.
Thrilling Tales of Dragon Slayers: a 3★ catalyst that gives the next character in up to +48% ATK. Proof a 3★ can be BiS.
